194	### Compiled tests
195	
196	Compiled tests are the `.test` files in `compiler_tests/`, `library_tests/` and `other_compiler_tests/`. They link with the library's jars in the tree's `default_repository/caches`. If a build started the caches again, or the tree's caches are empty, run the library order first (`build-and-caches.md`).
197	
198	The script is `explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh`. `climb-batch-N` is the folder's real name, not a placeholder. Run your own tree's copy: it runs the tree that it is in.
199	
200	    ONE_JVM=1 explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh <label> \
201	        ProjectFortress/compiler_tests X.test Y.test > <tree>/tmp/junit-<label>.txt 2>&1
202	
203	- `<label>` is any word. It marks the run's lines in the output. The script writes to standard output only, so redirect it to your `tmp/`.
204	- With `ONE_JVM=1`, the whole list runs in one `fortress junit` run, in one JVM. The compile and link tests run before the run tests, as in the suite. Without `ONE_JVM=1`, each file gets its own JVM.
205	- It removes the named components' entries from the tree's `default_repository/caches` before the whole list and after it, not between files. So a link test and the run test that uses its jar pass in one call, with or without `ONE_JVM=1`.
206	- It runs the classes in `ProjectFortress/build/` and builds nothing, as `harness-one.sh` does.
207	- It removes the Java stack frames, and cuts each line at 240 characters.
208	- Its JVMs keep their temporary files in the tree's `tmp/`, and run at `FORTRESS_THREADS=4`.

210	To run the same list in one JVM without the script, and without its removal of cache entries:
211	
212	    cd ProjectFortress && ../bin/fortress junit compiler_tests/X.test compiler_tests/Y.test

214	Run all the new files of one test folder together, in one JVM, as the suite does. A test that passes alone can fail beside others.

226	# The report and the record
227	
228	## What every report holds
229	
230	Your brief says where your report goes: a file that it names, your final message, or both. If it names no file, your report is your final message.
231	
232	A finding is something that your work learned about the tree or the language, and that the record does not hold yet. Examples: a defect, a behaviour that departs from the specification or from a decision of the curator, a measurement. What you did along the way is not a finding, for example the files that you read or edited. Your transcript keeps that.
233	
234	A fact is a finding that is an established property of the tree, the language, the library or their tools, and that later work builds on. A defect also gets its ledger row, and a fact about it may cite the row.
235	
236	A point to report is a kind of change or finding that the curator wants to review. Your brief names its points to report. Examples: a changed line of a test that the team wrote, a checker edit inside a change to the library, a changed line of the model program.
237	
238	Put each of these that you have in your report, in this form, whatever else your brief asks for:
239	
240	- **Defects.** Each defect that you measured, and the test or ledger row that records it (`tests-writing.md`, "How a defect is recorded").
241	- **Sentences of the specification made false.** Each sentence of the specification that your change makes false, quoted with its file and line. Such a sentence says what walk or the compiled path does. It is in the effect of an Appendix I entry (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex`), or in a `\revision` or `\note{}` box beside a passage.
242	- **Decisions.** Each choice that you made among alternatives, as a decision apart from the findings: what you chose, the alternatives, and the evidence, cited. If no decision of the curator covers it, say so, and say which reading you acted on. A decision left as a line inside the findings counts as not made.
243	- **Points to report.** Each point that your brief names and the work reached, with its evidence, also one that only part of the work reached.
244	- **For FACTS.** Each fact that your work established, in the hand-over form of "Writing to the record". If your brief let you write FACTS, give instead the number of each entry that you added or rewrote. If your work established no fact, write "none".
245	- **Commands.** Each command that you had to work out because this skill does not give it, with what it does.
246	- **Questions for the curator.** If something needs the curator's decision, list it as a decision not taken, in the form that `exploring.md` gives. The reader of your report brings it to the curator. Do not choose which of your items anyone reviews.
247	
248	## At a point to report
249	
250	- If the work reaches a point to report, do what the brief says for it. For example, a brief can say that a defect in the code is recorded in a ledger row and not repaired.
251	- Then finish the work.
252	- If a step cannot be undone, or would change a decision of the curator, report it instead. List it as a decision not taken, with its alternatives.
253	
254	## Timings and citations
255	
256	- If you take a timing that you will keep, run nothing else beside it. All agents of the session share the machine's cores (the `cloud-container` skill).
257	- Name the machine with every timing: `nproc`, the CPU's model and MHz, the load at start, the JDK, `FORTRESS_THREADS`. Only a pair of timings taken in one run measures a difference.
258	- If you take a measurement again because the code changed, say what changed.
259	- In a report, cite the tree at file:line, and quote results, two to five lines, each with its command. Never cite a file under `tmp/`.
260	
261	## POSITIONS and FACTS
262	
263	POSITIONS and FACTS describe the present: no dates, no names of who found what, no "corrected" or "superseded" notes. The history of each entry is in `POSITIONS-history.md` and `FACTS-history.md`, beside them. When your work needs the detail of an entry, print the report section that it cites (`$T 'doc:PATH#HEADING'`, below). Read its history only when the tree disagrees with the entry.
264	
265	Each entry is one line that starts with its permanent number: `F-87` in FACTS, `P-48` in POSITIONS. A FACTS entry is the fact as it stands now, what it means for the work, and the test that fails if the fact stops holding, under a bold title. If no test checks the fact, the entry gives the command and the output that show it. It points to the report section that holds the detail. Cite an entry by its number. If the reader must know what the entry says without printing it, add the first words of its title in quotes: F-87, "The first words ...".
266	
267	## The gap ledger
268	
269	The ledger's rows are the bug reports that the work fixes. A fix of a row starts with its reproduction, written as a test (`tests-writing.md`).
270	
271	A row is one line of eight cells, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of a topic section. Reports cite a row by its number, which it keeps for good. A new issue gets a new row.
272	
273	- Its status is one of seven words: `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`, `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`, `CONTESTED`, `RETIRED`, `FIXED`, `DUPLICATE`. The last three close a row. The row template (below) defines each.
274	- Its class is a kind and an area, such as `implementation gap (checker)`.
275	- The earlier text of a changed row is in `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger-history.md`.
276	
277	Read the ledger only through the queries below: it is too large to read whole.
278	
279	Three limits of `ledger.py` (below):
280	
281	- A row at its 1,200-character limit takes no further note.
282	- No command edits a row's claim. `close --claim` takes a corrected one.
283	- Its heading reader does not expand the specification's `\Trait{X}` macro. So a row that names a library trait's section cites `Specification-1.0-frozen/` by line.
284	
285	## Reading the record
286	
287	Read only the slice of the record that you need. This tool prints whole entries, in parts of bounded size:
288	
289	    T=explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh
290	
291	- `$T 'F-87'` prints one entry by its number, and `$T 'P-48'` one of POSITIONS. `$T 'F-87+'` adds each entry that F-87 cites by its number, and each entry that cites F-87. `$T 'history:F-87'` prints its history. Run one when your brief or a note cites an entry by its number.
292	- `$T 'positions:WORDS OF A TITLE'` prints one of the curator's decisions. Run it before you choose among ways to do something. If several titles hold the words, it names them.
293	- `$T 'WORDS OF A TITLE'` prints each FACTS entry whose bold title holds them, and `$T 'section:HEADING'` every entry of a FACTS section. Run one before you investigate a behaviour of the tree, and when your brief or a note names an entry. These queries and `positions:` read titles only: before you write that the record does not hold something, also grep FACTS and POSITIONS for its words.
294	- `$T 'index:WORDS'` prints the INDEX lines that hold the words. Run it to find the notes on a topic.
295	- `$T 'ledger-find:WORDS'` prints one line for each ledger row that holds every word. Run it when you meet a defect, before you investigate it.
296	- `$T 'ledger:ROW'` prints one row whole. Run it for each row that you need from a find, your brief or a note.
297	- `$T 'doc:PATH#HEADING'` prints a section of any note, or of a `.tex` chapter, and `$T 'map:FILE#HEADING'` a section of a note under `explorations/coordinator/map/`. Run one when your brief or a note names a section. `#HEADING@WORDS` prints only the table rows and list items of that section that hold every one of WORDS.
298	- `$T --check QUERY ...` prints only where each query matches and its size. Run it before a query whose size you do not know. `--part N` prints part N of a long output, and `--help` gives the rest.
299	
300	A word of a query that ends in `*` matches the start of a word. Any other word matches a whole word.
301	
302	Before you edit a file of the original tree, list the ledger rows that cite it, and read each row that your edit can change:
303	
304	    python3 explorations/coordinator/tools/ledger.py find --cites FILE
305	
306	## Writing to the record
307	
308	- Write FACTS and POSITIONS only with `explorations/coordinator/tools/record.py`, never by hand. `add` gives a new entry its number, and `set` rewrites an entry. The tool writes the entry to `FACTS.md` or `POSITIONS.md`, and its earlier text to the history file beside it. It commits nothing: commit both files in one commit. Its header gives its usage.
309	- If your brief lets you write FACTS, add each fact as a new entry in the section of its topic, in the commit that establishes it. Put its detail in a section of your report: the file:line citations, the commands with their output, and the measured numbers. Point the entry to that section, by your report's file and the section's heading. If your report is only your final message, hand the fact over instead. Spend no effort on the entry's wording: it is rewritten to the record's form after your work.
310	- If your brief does not let you write FACTS, hand each fact over in the "For FACTS" item of your report, with:
311	  - the fact as it stands now, in one sentence;
312	  - what it means for the work;
313	  - the number that a decision rests on, if any, with what it counts; if its parts belong to different ledger rows, the part of each row;
314	  - the test that fails if the fact stops holding, or the command and the output that show it;
315	  - the section of your report that holds the detail.

<!-- Whether the revival must build the team's unfinished "where" feature to reach the switch-over: of the thirteen checker errors filed as waiting on it, twelve go away with ordinary edits of the library that change no answer microGPT or the walk tests compute (one revival test of the removed declarations aside), and the thirteenth, the ordering of lists, needs a list to count as ordered only when its elements are ordered, which the library cannot say today. -->

The probe worker returned this text when the harness refused it a report file; the coordinating session wrote it here unchanged on 2026-10-16. The worktree `/home/user/fortress-probe-where` holds the patches and the new tests.

# `where` clauses and the distance to the switch-over: a measurement

This is a measurement probe on the branch `wip/probe-where-clauses`, in the worktree `/home/user/fortress-probe-where`. The worktree was seeded from the base build `/home/user/fortress-base16` (`528438ac5`; `main` at `d731fc328` has changed no code since). The edits are uncommitted in the worktree; the patches are quoted inline below. There are two parts, written in this order and kept apart:

- **Part A** is the brief: library edits that use no new language, and what the code generator does with `NatParam`'s clause. Part A was finished and written before Part B began.
- **Part B** is the curator's addition, sent mid-task: the narrow `where`-clause forms, built as shadow patches in the compiled checker.

---

# Part A: library edits with no new language

## A.0 In short

| Group (ledger row) | Errors | Cause | Library edit that clears it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SUM`'s fusion pairs with `MAX` and `MIN` (433) | 6 | Four errors: `SumReduction` (bound `AdditiveGroup`) names `MaxReduction[\T\]`, `MinReduction[\T\]` and their pairs, whose bounds it does not meet. Two errors: the `distribute` overloads answer a pair over `Maybe[\T\]`, where the inherited `distribute` answers a pair over `T`. No bound fixes those two. | **Yes: removal.** Only the team's experimental `Generator2` reaches these declarations, and none of its answers change. A `where` clause would clear only 4 of the 6. |
| `AnyList`'s `\|\|`, `addLeft`, `addRight`, and the list comprehension's unwrap (636) | 4 | `AnyList` and `AnyCovColl` are supertraits with no element type. Their bodies call functions that need a `List[\E\]` or a `CovariantCollection[\T\]`. | **Yes.** `\|\|` moves into `List[\E\]` through one private generic helper. `addLeft`/`addRight` become `singleton(e) \|\| self`. The unwrap takes `cast[\CovariantCollection[\T\]\]`. Walk prints the same 14 lines on a probe before and after. |
| The identities' numeral fallback (436) | 2 | `else => 0` and `else => 1` answer a numeral where `T` is declared. | **Yes, for the checker:** `cast[\T\](0)` and `cast[\T\](1)`, the device the branches above already use. Row 436's own defect (an empty sum over a non-number group has no zero) stays. |
| `LexicographicOrder`'s `CMP` (634, list half) | 1 | `a CMP b` on values of the unbounded element type `E`. | **No.** Each device loses something the judgement on record weighed. Clearing it needs a list to be ordered exactly when its elements are: conditional extension. |

- **Distance with all three edits: 49 to 37.** Exactly the twelve sites above go, and none appear.
- **Walk:** all 621 tests of `ProjectFortress/tests`, run in one JVM, give 2 failures. The base fails the same two with the same seed, and both pass when run alone. One revival test, `GeneratorDeclarations.fss`, needed three lines changed. microGPT's quick pair passes 7 of 7 checks each.
- **The code generator on `NatParam`:** it refuses the trait at its guard, "Can't compile TraitDecl" (`CodeGen.java:5027-5033`). With only that guard relaxed in a scratch copy, a trait with a bindings-only clause compiles and runs. Opening a value at a call then fails the JVM's verifier.

## A.1 The thirteen errors, traced

The sites are rows of `explorations/compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv`. Line numbers are `main`'s.

**Row 433, six errors** (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss`):

1. `wellformed`, `:3421`. `distribute(r: MaxReduction[\T\])` sits in `object SumReduction[\T extends AdditiveGroup[\T\]\]` (`:3417`). `MaxReduction`'s bound is `StandardMax[\T\]` (`:3456`).
2. `wellformed`, `:3423`. The same with `MinReduction` (bound `StandardMin`, `:3447`).
3. `wellformed`, reported at `:3405`, for the body `MaxSumReductionPair[\T\]` at `:3422`. The checker reports a call's unmet bound at the callee's declaration (ledger row 720).
4. `wellformed`, reported at `:3411`, for `MinSumReductionPair[\T\]` at `:3424`.
5. `return-type`, `:3421` against `:3233`. The overload answers `PossibleReductionPair[\Maybe[\T\]\]`. The inherited `distribute(r: Any)` of `ActualReduction[\R,L\]` answers `PossibleReductionPair[\T\]`. Static parameters are invariant, so the overload's result does not fit the inherited one.
6. `return-type`, `:3423`. The same for the `MinReduction` overload.

Errors 5 and 6 do not depend on any bound. I wrote a scratch component of the same shape with no bound anywhere (`tmp/probe/rt/LiftedPairReturn.fss`) and it gets the same refusal:

    trait Red[\R,L\]  distribute(r: Any): Pair[\R\] = NoPair[\R\]  end
    object Mx[\T\] extends Red[\T, Lifted[\T\]\] end
    object Sm[\T\] extends Red[\T,T\]
        distribute(r: Mx[\T\]): Pair[\Lifted[\T\]\] = SomePair[\Lifted[\T\]\]
    end

    $ bin/fortress compile LiftedPairReturn.fss
        For distribute,
    the return type of (Sm[\T\], Mx[\T\])->Pair[\Lifted[\T\]\] @ ...:15:5-73 should be a subtype of the
        return type of (Red[\T,T\], Any)->Pair[\T\] @ ...:11:5-47
    File LiftedPairReturn.fss has 1 error.

So the ledger's designed fix, a `where` clause per overload (row 433's notes), would clear errors 1 to 4 and leave 5 and 6.

The team saw the underlying problem: "This lifting type should be replaced with the type L of ReductionPair[\R, L\] returned by r.distribute(q). But, we do not have any way to capture the type L...." (`Library/Generator2.fss:170-173`, Emoto 2009, present at `a874948ac`).

**Row 636, four errors** (`Library/List.fss`):

7. `:88`, `app(self,f)` in `trait AnyList`. `self` and `f` are `AnyList`s, and `app` takes `List[\E\]` and `List[\F\]` (`:93`). The team's comment that would have said every `AnyList` is a `List[\E\]`, "comprises List[\E\] where [\E\]", remains a comment (`:87`; `List.fsi:56`, "Not yet").
8. `:89`, `addL(e,self)`, for the same reason (`:102`).
9. `:90`, `addR(self,e)`, for the same reason (`:105`).
10. `:179`, `cc.toImmutableArray()` on an `AnyCovColl`. `toImmutableArray` belongs to `CovariantCollection[\T\]` (`Library/CovariantCollection.fss:71-78`, `:144-146`).

**Row 436, two errors:**

11. `FortressLibrary.fss:3367`, `additiveIdentity`: body type `OR(IntLiteral,T)`, from `else => 0` at `:3380`.
12. `:3384`, `multiplicativeIdentity`: the same, from `else => 1` at `:3397`.

**Row 634, list half, one error:**

13. `FortressLibrary.fss:2063`, `fn(a:E,b:E): TotalComparison => a CMP b` in `LexicographicOrder[\T extends LexicographicOrder[\T,E\],E\]` (`:2058`). `E` is unbounded, and `List[\E\]` extends it at every `E` (`List.fss:112`).

## A.2 The edits, built as shadow patches

### A.2.1 Row 433: remove the `MAX`/`MIN` fusion with `SUM`

I removed these from `FortressLibrary.fss`:

- `MaxSumReductionPair` (`:3405-3409`) and `MinSumReductionPair` (`:3411-3415`).
- `SumReduction`'s two `distribute` overloads (`:3421-3424`).
- `LiftedCommutativeMonoidReduction` (`:3283-3309`), which only the two pairs used.

None of them is in the api.

**What reaches them.** `Generator2.fss:73`'s `r.distribute(q)` and its theorems for `inits`, `tails` and `segs`, reached through `Generator2.generate2` (`FortressLibrary.fss:4743`) from `__bigOperator2`'s fused arm (`:1468-1473`). Also the revival's `GeneratorDeclarations.fss`.

**What moves under walk.** `SumReduction[\ZZ32\].distribute(MaxReduction[\ZZ32\])` now answers `NoReductionPair`. As it stood, `GeneratorDeclarations` failed on that: "FAIL: J7/0:Nothing =/= J7/0:Just(5)". I changed three of its lines:

    -    some = SumReduction[\ZZ32\].distribute(MaxReduction[\ZZ32\])
    +    some = ProdReduction[\ZZ32\].distribute(SumReduction[\ZZ32\])
    -    assert(some.inner.empty().asString, "Just(0)", ...)
    -    assert(some.inner.join(Just[\ZZ32\](2), Just[\ZZ32\](3)).asString, "Just(5)", ...)
    +    assert(SumReduction[\ZZ32\].distribute(MaxReduction[\ZZ32\]).holds, false, "the sum has no fusion pair with the maximum")

**What does not move.** The team's `Generator2Test.fss` still prints `res = 46, ggres = 46`, `15, 15`, `8, 8` and passes. `fusedMax` still asserts 6, 4, 6, 4 and 5.

**Cost.** Emoto's fast path for the maximum or minimum of sums over a generator of generators is gone. Walk now computes those the naive way, with the same answers. The `PROD`-over-`SUM` fusion stays.

**Why no other device works.**

- A narrower bound would refuse `SUM` over every unordered group.
- Moving the overloads into `MaxReduction` does not help, because `T` lacks `AdditiveGroup` there.
- A per-type witness `typecase` can name `MaxSumReductionPair[\ZZ32\]`. But the method must still answer `PossibleReductionPair[\T\]`, so errors 5 and 6 stay, and a cast to that type would be false at run time.
- The team's own attempt, `distribute[\K\](r: ActualReduction[\R,K\])`, is commented out beside "a hack to avoid the error of overloaded methods" (`:3232-3237`; also `Generator2.fss:75-84`).

### A.2.2 Row 636: put `AnyList`'s bodies where the element type is known

    @@ Library/List.fss, trait AnyList
    -    opr ||(self, f:AnyList): AnyList = app(self,f)
    -    addLeft(e:Any): AnyList = addL(e,self)
    -    addRight(e:Any): AnyList = addR(self,e)
    +    opr ||(self, f:AnyList): AnyList = self.appendAny(f)
    +    addLeft(e:Any): AnyList = singleton(e) || self
    +    addRight(e:Any): AnyList = self || singleton(e)
    +    private appendAny(f:AnyList): AnyList
    +    private appendedTo[\D\](a:List[\D\]): AnyList
    @@ (addL and addR, now unused, removed)
    @@ trait List[\E\]
    +    private appendAny(f:AnyList): AnyList = f.appendedTo[\E\](self)
    +    private appendedTo[\D\](a:List[\D\]): AnyList = app(a,self)
    @@ opr BIG <|[\T\]|>
    -    ... fn (cc) => fromImmutableArray(cc.toImmutableArray()))
    +    ... fn (cc) => fromImmutableArray(cast[\CovariantCollection[\T\]\](cc).toImmutableArray()))

This is double dispatch through private generic methods. `List` already uses the same shape for `appendRC[\T\]` and its relatives (`List.fss:130-133`). `cast` is the library's run-time check (`FortressLibrary.fss:33-37`), and `List.fss:313` already uses it. The api is unchanged.

- **What it clears.** All four. A distance run over List alone takes List from 5 errors to 1; the one left is site 40, which is not among the thirteen.
- **Why not `addL(e,self)` inside `List`.** The checker still refuses it there ("not applicable to an argument of type (Any, List.List[\E\])"). Writing `addL[\Any,Any,E\]` would make walk's result a `List[\Any\]` instead of the join of the two element types.
- **What moves under walk.** Nothing. A probe of 14 values printed each list and which of `List[\ZZ32\]`/`Number`/`Object`/`Any` it is. The cases: heterogeneous `||`, `addLeft("y")` and `addRight(2.5)` on a `List[\ZZ32\]`, typed, untyped, empty and filtered comprehensions. The base and the edit print identical output (for example `e = <|1, 2, 2.5|> ZZ32:false Number:true Object:false Any:false`).
- **Cost.** Two private abstract methods on `AnyList`, two bodies on `List`, one more dispatch on a heterogeneous `||`, and a run-time check in every list comprehension's unwrap. No test or probe trips that check.

### A.2.3 Row 436: cast the fallback

    -        else => 0
    +        else => cast[\T\](0)
    -        else => 1
    +        else => cast[\T\](1)

- **What it clears.** Both errors.
- **What moves under walk.** Only runs that reach the fallback, which means a non-number `T`. There the numeral was never a `T` anyway. `XXXEmptyGroupSumRungF` stays an expected failure: on the base it raises a `ProgramError` at `FortressLibrary.fss:1315`, on the edit `FortressException: CastError`; both report "OK Saw expected exception".
- **What it leaves.** The empty sum's missing zero. Fixing that is `HasIdentity` (A.6, B.4).

### A.2.4 Row 634's list half: no edit works

I checked each device against `explorations/reviews/tuple-comparisons-judgement.md` section 2:

- **Bound `LexicographicOrder`'s `E`** (its way 1c). Every `List[\E\]` would then need an ordered `E`, so lists of tuples, functions and `()` would be refused, against P-42, and the pins in `ResultBoundsRungB.fss:48-59` would stop.

## A.5 The walk folder in one JVM

To keep to one JVM, I ran the folder as a single `SystemJUTest` instead of four shards.

- **Failures.** 2 of 621: `ReflectTest` and `ReflectiveQuickCheckTest`. Both stop with "Failed to find any matching overload, args = (NodeSet[\(String,Type)\],NodeSet[\(String,Type)\])" at `Library/Set.fss:124:46`, and the overload set lists a `CUP ... [no type]` entry.

- **Not recorded.** No ledger row holds it.

## A.6 What the team left, and the smallest piece of language

**Row 634's list half.** What the team left:

- The grammar: `TraitTypeWhere(BaseType, Option<WhereClause>)` (`Fortress.ast:1697`).
- A test that only parses the form, `tests/conditionalExtension.fss`. Per the curator, it is a superseded design.
- The specification's sentence on comparing lists "whose elements support these same comparison operators" (`opr-overview.tex:294-295`) and `algebraic-constraints.tex:520-523`.
- "where clauses and conditional extension" in the list of unsupported features (`preamble.tex:95`).
- No rule for when such an extension holds.

The smallest piece of language is conditional extension of one trait: `List[\E\] extends LexicographicOrder[\List[\E\],E\] where { E extends StandardTotalOrder[\E\] }`, with `E` bounded. The checker's hierarchy, walk's dispatch and the code generator would each read the condition. Part B, item 3, builds the checker's half.

**The other three groups, had the team's own design been wanted:**

- **Row 433:** method `where` clauses, plus a way to name the pair's lifted type. For the second, the team left only the commented generic method and Emoto's comment.
- **Row 636:** the comment `comprises List[\E\] where [\E\]` (`List.fsi:56`, `List.fss:87`), with the checker opening an `AnyList` as a `List[\E\]` at a fresh `E`. Today it opens only `nat`/`int` variables (F-121, F-146). The api adds: "This should not be necessary in the presence of true type inference." (`List.fsi:50-54`).

The clause is `trait NatParam comprises { N[\n\] } where [\ nat n \]` (`NatReflect.fsi:23`, `.fss:24`). The team wrote it as a comment and the revival restored it (`7fd8fddc8`). The parser stores it as the trait header's `whereClause`, with bindings and no constraints (`Fortress.ast:1429-1430`).

The code generator's guards (`CodeGen.java`):

- `forTraitDecl` requires `getWhereClause().isNone()`, no throws clause and no contract (`:5023-5033`).
- Objects have the same guard (`:4105-4115`).
- Functions and methods have it too: "Don't know how to compile this kind of FnDecl." (`:2965-2976`).

Past the guards, the code generator already passes a declaration's where clause to its type analyzer (`:1878`, `:5106`).

A six-line component (`tmp/probe/np/NatParamWhere.fss`) compiles through the checker and stops in the code generator:

    trait NatP comprises { Nn[\n\] } where [\ nat n \]
    end
    value object Nn[\nat n\] extends NatP end

            at ...CodeGen.forTraitDecl(CodeGen.java:5033)

- `NatParamWhere` compiles and runs (`PASS`).
- The gated `compiler_tests/XXXNatOpenRun.fss` compiles, then fails verification: `java.lang.VerifyError: Bad type on operand stack ... Type 'XXXNatOpenRun$NatParamT' ... is not assignable to 'XXXNatOpenRun$Nt?n#3?'`. The call passes the trait value with no class test and no size read: the open half of F-146 and row 307.

So for `NatParam` the code generator needs two things: the guard relaxed for bindings-only clauses, and code that opens a value at a call.

## A.8 Decisions, defects, hand-overs (Part A)

**Decisions** (no POSITIONS entry covers any of them):

1. Row 433 by removal. No typecase can clear errors 5 and 6.
2. `LiftedCommutativeMonoidReduction` removed too. Nothing else uses it, and the test cannot name it (walk: "Function LiftedCommutativeMonoidReduction is not defined.").
3. Row 636 through private helpers rather than making `AnyList`'s methods abstract, which would touch `List.fsi`.
4. `cast[\T\](0)` rather than `throw`, matching the branches above it.
5. The walk folder as one JVM, and microGPT's pair run sequentially; `mg-run.sh` starts both at once.

**Defects.** The walk folder in one JVM fails `ReflectTest` and `ReflectiveQuickCheckTest` on the base too (A.5). It needs a ledger row: way 3, reproducer none, with the command and seed of A.5 in the notes.

**For FACTS.**

- Two of row 433's errors are the overloading rule over invariant static parameters, not an unmet bound, so a method `where` clause clears 4 of the 6 (A.1, with its command and output).
- Twelve of the thirteen errors clear with library edits, taking the distance from 49 to 37 with nothing new (A.4).
- The code generator refuses `NatParam`'s clause only at the trait guard; past it, opening a value at a call fails verification (A.7).

**Commands worked out.**

- One-JVM walk folder, from `ProjectFortress/`: `FORTRESS_THREADS=4 FORTRESS_JUNIT_VERBOSE=1 FORTRESS_CACHES=<c> nice -n 19 java -Xmx768m -Xss32m -Djava.io.tmpdir=<t> -Dfortress.caches=<c> -Dtests=<tree>/ProjectFortress/tests [-Dfortress.unittests.seed=S] -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -cp "$(bin/fortress_classpath|tail -1)" com.sun.fortress.tests.unit_tests.SystemJUTest`. It takes 206 to 294 s. Delete `ProjectFortress/testFile.txt` afterwards.
- The distance stage over one component: a copy of `run.sh` with `COMPONENTS` set. About 120 to 140 s for List.
- microGPT one program at a time: a copy of `mg-run.sh` with an absolute `cd` and no `&`.

**Questions for the curator.**

- Row 433: remove the `MAX`/`MIN` fusion (every answer stays the same; the fast path goes), or keep it and wait for a design of `distribute`'s result type that nothing the team left supplies.
- Row 436: does the missing zero wait for `HasIdentity`?

# Part B: the narrow `where`-clause forms, as shadow patches in the checker

I built these by compiling the changed Scala and Java files with `scalac`/`javac` and copying the classes over the worktree's `ProjectFortress/build`. The originals are saved in `tmp/build-orig/classes.tar`. I did not use ant. The full checker diff is `tmp/partB-checker-final.patch` (353 lines). I wrote every test first and saw it fail on the unpatched checker.

## B.0 In short

| Form | Clears, with the team's spelling in the library | Soundness tests | Hole measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. A type variable in a `comprises` clause, opened at a call (`AnyList`) | `app(self,f)`: 1 of row 636's 4 | escape refused; two values not taken as one; the Amin–Tate shape refused | none in this form |
| 2. A `where` constraint read as a bound (row 677) | row 433's 4 `wellformed` errors; its 2 `return-type` errors stay, as A.1 predicted | calls with an unmet constraint on the function's own parameter are refused | a constraint on the enclosing trait's parameter is not checked at a dotted call |
| 3. Conditional extension, by the accepted rule | row 634's `CMP` | lists of numbers and of strings compare; a list of functions does not; a vector of numbers adds, a vector of strings does not | a member checked under the condition stays callable where the condition fails |
| 4. `HasIdentity` | not built: it needs a `coerces` constraint, a fourth kind of clause | — | — |

**Distance runs:**

- **All forms, with the team's spellings and no Part A edits: 49 to 43.** Six sites clear: 433's 4, 636's `app`, 634's `CMP`. Nothing new appears beyond two array errors whose union members swapped order. Still open: 433's 2 return-type errors, `addL`/`addR`, the comprehension, and 436's 2.
- **Part A plus only the form it could not avoid (conditional extension): 37 to 36.** `CMP` clears and nothing is new. So all thirteen are cleared by Part A plus conditional extension.

**Tests:**

- The compiler track (`CompilerJUTest` in one JVM): 1221 tests, 3 failures. These are the three red tests below that mark holes or a promotion. Every other test passes, including the `NatOpen*` tests.
- The library track: `OK (86 tests)`. The other-compiler track: `OK (263 tests)`. Both counts match batch 15b.
- Walk, on both Part B libraries: 19 where-clause, list and generator tests give `OK (19 tests)`.
- The whole walk folder on Part A plus conditional extension: 621 tests, the same 2 failures as the base.
- microGPT on Part A plus conditional extension: 7 of 7 each.

## B.1 A type variable opened from a `comprises` clause

**Lines changed** (worktree):

- `TypeDisambiguator.java:88-99, 111, 115-116, 120, 122`: a trait's `where`-bound type variables are in scope in its `comprises` clause, self type, parameters and members, but not in its extends clause. Without this, "E is undefined." The self type and the `self` parameters carry the comprised types.
- `TypeAnalyzer.scala:820-824`: `whereSizes` now includes type bindings.

- `TypeAnalyzer.scala:808, 911`: the arguments are passed through.

- `KindEnv.scala:79-81, 111-118`: a registry of opened names, found from every environment.

#!/bin/bash
# The gate's distance stage: the compiled checker over the whole interpreter library, the
# twelve prelude apis and their twelve components, every stage of every unit run whatever
# the earlier stages reported, so that nothing hides behind an early return; one table.
#
# Why it exists: Pavol's answer 11 (POSITIONS.md, 2026-09-26): the full measurement of the
# distance to the switch-over "becomes a report-only stage of phase 3's gates, whose job is
# driving it down". The checker-count stage beside it (../checker-count/run.sh) sees only
# the errors before each api's early return, 62 of about 1,740 on 2026-09-27.
#
# Run from $FORTRESS_HOME with explorations/experiment/env.sh sourced, after ant compileAll:
#
#     explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/run.sh <out-file> [scratch-dir] [setting]
#
# It writes the table to <out-file> and prints it. Nothing in the tree is touched: the
# shadow sources and classes, the driver, the checker's caches (-Dfortress.caches) and the
# JVM's temporary directory (so Rats! leaves nothing in /tmp) go to the scratch directory
# (default: $TMPDIR or /tmp), and the caches are deleted at the end. It never removes
# /tmp/fortress*rats, which other runs on the machine use. Exit 0 if the table was
# produced, 1 if it could not be. One JVM, -Xmx4g, one busy core: 789 s on the idle 4-CPU
# container on 2026-09-27, 14 to 24 minutes under load 7 to 18 (switch-over-distance-flat.md
# section 5); the table's #seconds and #machine rows say what each run took and where.
#
# The setting: "any" by default, the compiled path with the implicit bound Any
# (DistanceMulti's -setting any: the extends-Object pre-desugaring off, as walk's, and the
# compiled-expression desugaring on, as the compile path's). Answer 11 names the compile
# path's setting; batch 7's question 1, answered (a) on 2026-09-27 (POSITIONS.md, the
# numerics plans), bounds an unbounded type parameter by Any, and under it the switch-over
# takes that bound for the compiled path (CLIMB-BATCH-7.md section 1, Q1), so the 372
# "bound Object" errors of the plain compile setting are the setting's, not the library's
# (switch-over-distance-flat.md sections 2.7 and 5: "under (a) the stage runs stage-any").
# On the tree of 2026-09-27 it differs from walk's setting by the compiled-expression
# desugaring's 12 abstract-method errors on bodyless functions, one export error and the
# variance checker's crash on Stream: 1,746 to 1,747 against 1,737 to 1,738 (FACTS.md,
# "The true distance to the switch-over"). The third argument, walk or compile, runs
# another setting, for a comparison with the measurements on file; the gate never passes it.
#
# The overloading checker's memo is off (-Dfortress.analyzer.overload.cache=false), as in
# every run of the measurement: keyed on declaration pairs, it hides 27 to 35 errors
# depending on the build order (FACTS.md, "The overloading checker's memo hides errors
# by build order, so every count runs with it off ...").
#
# The sources beside this script are copies, taken 2026-09-27, so that the gate does not
# depend on a probe directory, as the checker-count stage's were: DistanceMulti.java from
# perf-probes/prelude/switch-over-distance-flat/ (35ef70584); shadow-patch.py from
# perf-probes/prelude/desugar-codegen/ (e5d8cdbd2); add-patch.py and errors.py from
# perf-probes/prelude/switch-over-distance/ (a7e3df9ad, 14d2f9839); classify.py from
# perf-probes/prelude/distance-triage/ (e17a9badc); all unchanged but classify.py, which since
# row 577 finds the library places that name three of its classes by their declarations in
# the tree's sources ($FH, passed to table.py), not by line ranges. table.py is new: it
# counts as those scripts count and prints the rows below. The shadow classes are not
# copies: they are made from the tracked sources at every run by text edits that must each
# match exactly once (shadow-patch.py, add-patch.py), so there is no copied checker to go
# stale silently; an edit that no longer matches stops the run before the checker starts,
# and the table then says so in its #shadow row, with no counts.
#
# The table, tab-separated, every row tagged:
#   #distance   the setting, the switches and the twelve targets
#   #total      distinct errors
#   #kind       by kind (errors.py): exclusion, comprises, overloading, return-type, ...
#   #class      by root cause (classify.py, distance-triage.md section 2), with its name
#   #check      a disagreement: errors.py's and table.py's totals, or sites classify.py cannot
#               find in the tree's library source
#   #unit       by the unit that printed the error first
#   #crash      each declaration, stage or target the checker crashed on
#   #seconds    the run's wall time, and FortressLibrary's, the part that takes it
#   #machine    nproc, CPU model and MHz, load at start, JDK, FORTRESS_THREADS
#   #shadow     whether every shadow edit matched the tracked sources; the last row
# ../distance/compare.sh compares two tables. The run-to-run variation is 2 to 4 errors,
# in the comparisons' and Maybe's pairs and the joins of array bodies (switch-over-
# distance-flat.md section 5).
set -u

OUT=${1:-}
if [ -z "$OUT" ] ; then echo "usage: $0 <out-file> [scratch-dir] [any|walk|compile]" >&2 ; exit 1 ; fi
case "$OUT" in /*) ;; *) OUT="$PWD/$OUT" ;; esac
FH=${FORTRESS_HOME:-$PWD}
D="$FH/explorations/coordinator/tools/distance"
SCRATCH=${2:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/distance.$$}
case "$SCRATCH" in /*) ;; *) SCRATCH="$PWD/$SCRATCH" ;; esac
SETTING=${3:-any}
case "$SETTING" in any|walk|compile) ;; *) echo "distance: unknown setting $SETTING" >&2 ; exit 1 ;; esac
FLAGS="-Dprobe.tolerant=true -Dprobe.all=true -Dfortress.analyzer.overload.cache=false"
COMPONENTS="Library/FortressLibrary.fss Library/RangeInternals.fss ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss
 ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/NativeArray.fss Library/List.fss Library/String.fss Library/FlatString.fss Library/Stream.fss
 ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/NatReflect.fss Library/TypeProxy.fss Library/Writer.fss ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/AnyType.fss"

rm -rf "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes" "$SCRATCH/classes" "$SCRATCH/caches" "$SCRATCH/tmp"
mkdir -p "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes" "$SCRATCH/classes" "$SCRATCH/caches" "$SCRATCH/tmp" \
         "$(dirname "$OUT")" || exit 1
CP=$("$FH/bin/fortress_classpath" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | sed 's#:[^:]*/default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache##')
if [ -z "$CP" ] ; then echo "distance: no classpath from bin/fortress_classpath" >&2 ; exit 1 ; fi
MACHINE="nproc=$(nproc); $(grep -m1 'model name' /proc/cpuinfo | sed 's/^[^:]*: *//'); $(grep -m1 'cpu MHz' /proc/cpuinfo | sed 's/^[^:]*: *//') MHz; load at start $(cut -d' ' -f1-3 /proc/loadavg); $(java -version 2>&1 | head -1); FORTRESS_THREADS=${FORTRESS_THREADS:-unset}"

# 1. the shadows, from the tracked sources (perf-probes/prelude/switch-over-distance/make-shadows.sh's
#    steps), and the driver; a text edit that no longer matches is the one way this can go stale
SHADOW="every shadow edit matched the tracked sources"
if ! ( cd "$FH" && python3 "$D/shadow-patch.py" ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" \
                && python3 "$D/add-patch.py" "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" ) > "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" 2>&1 ; then
    SHADOW="STALE: a shadow edit no longer matches the tracked sources: $(grep -E '^AssertionError' "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" | tail -1 | tr -s ' ' | cut -c1-200); see $SCRATCH/shadows.txt"
elif ! javac -nowarn -encoding UTF-8 -cp "$CP" -d "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/TypeCheckPhase.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/DesugarPhase.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/CodeGenerationPhase.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/Desugarer.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/nodes_util/NodeComparator.java" >> "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" 2>&1 ; then
    SHADOW="STALE: the shadow sources no longer compile against the tree; see $SCRATCH/shadows.txt"
elif ! javac -nowarn -cp "$CP" -d "$SCRATCH/classes" "$D/DistanceMulti.java" >> "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" 2>&1 ; then
    SHADOW="STALE: DistanceMulti.java no longer compiles against the tree; see $SCRATCH/shadows.txt"
fi

# 2. the run: one JVM, the twelve components, FortressLibrary first so that its run checks
#    the twelve apis with every stage (DistanceMulti.java's header)
RC=
case "$SHADOW" in
  STALE*) : > "$SCRATCH/run.txt" ;;
  *) S=$(date +%s)
     ( cd "$FH" && timeout -k 30 5400 java -Xmx4g -Xss64m -XX:-OmitStackTraceInFastThrow \
           -Djava.io.tmpdir="$SCRATCH/tmp" -Dfortress.caches="$SCRATCH/caches" $FLAGS \
           -cp "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes:$SCRATCH/classes:$CP" DistanceMulti -order check -setting "$SETTING" $COMPONENTS
     ) > "$SCRATCH/run.txt" 2>&1
     RC=$? ; ELAPSED=$(( $(date +%s) - S ))
     rm -rf "$SCRATCH/caches" "$SCRATCH/tmp" ;;
esac

# 3. the table. errors.py's tally and its one-row-per-error list stay in the scratch
#    directory for whoever needs the sites (compare-sites, the review); table.py's rows go
#    into the table, and their total is checked against errors.py's own count.
{
    printf '#distance\tsetting %s; %s; %s\n' "$SETTING" "$FLAGS" "$(echo $COMPONENTS | wc -w) components in one JVM (DistanceMulti -order check)"
    if grep -q '^### all seconds=' "$SCRATCH/run.txt" ; then
        python3 -B "$D/table.py" "$SCRATCH/run.txt" "$FH" > "$SCRATCH/rows.txt" 2>&1
        cat "$SCRATCH/rows.txt"
        python3 "$D/errors.py" "$SCRATCH/errors.tsv" "$SCRATCH/run.txt" > "$SCRATCH/tally.txt" 2>&1
        E=$(sed -n 's/^# \([0-9]*\) distinct errors.*/\1/p' "$SCRATCH/tally.txt")
        T=$(awk -F'\t' '$1 == "#total" { print $2 }' "$SCRATCH/rows.txt")
        [ "$E" = "$T" ] || printf '#check\terrors.py counts %s, table.py %s: the two normalisations differ on this run; see %s\n' "$E" "$T" "$SCRATCH/tally.txt"
        printf '#seconds\t%s\tFortressLibrary %s\n' "${ELAPSED:-?}" "$(sed -n 's/^### done Library\/FortressLibrary.fss rc=[0-9]* seconds=\([0-9]*\)$/\1/p' "$SCRATCH/run.txt")"
    else
        case "$SHADOW" in
          STALE*) printf '#total\tnone: the checker did not run\n' ;;
          *) printf '#total\tnone: the run ended without its last line (rc=%s); see %s\n' "${RC:-?}" "$SCRATCH/run.txt" ;;
        esac
    fi
    printf '#machine\t%s\n' "$MACHINE"
    printf '#shadow\t%s\n' "$SHADOW"
} > "$OUT"

cat "$OUT"
echo "# distance: full output $SCRATCH/run.txt, rc=${RC:-not run}; errors.py's tally $SCRATCH/tally.txt"
grep -q '^#total	[0-9]' "$OUT"
#!/bin/bash
# The distance stage's comparison: this table (run.sh's) against the last landed one.
#
#     explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/compare.sh <last-landed-table|""> <this-table>
#
# Prints one verdict line, then every #kind and #class row whose count moved, with the
# change, and every #crash row that went or came. It is REPORTED and never red: it always
# exits 0, whatever moved, a stale shadow and a run that produced no table included (Pavol,
# answer 11, POSITIONS.md 2026-09-26: a report-only stage, whose job is driving the distance
# down). The verdicts:
#   DISTANCE DOWN|UP|SAME   <last> -> <now>
#   DISTANCE FIRST          no landed table to compare with
#   DISTANCE NO TABLE       this run produced no count, with the table's own reason
#   SETTING CHANGED         the two tables ran different settings: the counts are not like for like
#   SHADOW STALE            a shadow edit no longer matches the tracked sources
# A move of 2 to 4 errors in the components' type errors or in which pair of LEXICO, SQCAP or
# INVERSE declarations an overloading error names is the checker's run-to-run variation
# (switch-over-distance-flat.md section 5), not a change; a crash row whose line numbers
# moved because a rung edited above it prints as one gone and one new.
set -u
OLD=${1:-}; NEW=${2:?usage: compare.sh <last-landed-table> <this-table>}
field () { awk -F'\t' -v t="$1" '$1 == t { sub("^[^\t]*\t", ""); print; exit }' "$2" ; }

now=$(field '#total' "$NEW")
sh=$(field '#shadow' "$NEW")
case "$sh" in STALE*) echo "SHADOW STALE   ${sh#STALE: }" ;; esac
case "$now" in
  ''|none*) echo "DISTANCE NO TABLE   ${now:-no #total row}" ; exit 0 ;;
esac
if [ -z "$OLD" ] || [ ! -f "$OLD" ] ; then
    echo "DISTANCE FIRST   $now distinct errors, $(field '#distance' "$NEW" | cut -d';' -f1); no landed table to compare with"
    exit 0
fi
was=$(field '#total' "$OLD")
ws=$(field '#distance' "$OLD" | cut -d';' -f1); ns=$(field '#distance' "$NEW" | cut -d';' -f1)
[ "$ws" = "$ns" ] || echo "SETTING CHANGED   was $ws, now $ns: the counts below are not like for like"
case "$was" in ''|none*) echo "DISTANCE $now, the landed table has no count (${was:-no #total row})" ; exit 0 ;; esac
if   [ "$now" -lt "$was" ] ; then echo "DISTANCE DOWN   $was -> $now ($((now - was)))"
elif [ "$now" -gt "$was" ] ; then echo "DISTANCE UP   $was -> $now (+$((now - was)))"
else echo "DISTANCE SAME   $now" ; fi
awk -F'\t' '
  function key(r) { return $1 == "#kind" || $1 == "#class" || $1 == "#unit" }
  FNR == NR { if (key()) { k = substr($1, 2) " " $2 ; a[k] = $3 ; nm[k] = $4 ; ord[++n] = k }
              else if ($1 == "#crash") ca[$0] = 1 ; next }
  key() { k = substr($1, 2) " " $2 ; b[k] = $3 ; nm[k] = $4 ; if (!(k in a)) ord[++n] = k }
  $1 == "#crash" { cb[$0] = 1 }
  END {
    for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) { k = ord[i] ; if (seen[k]++) continue
      d = (b[k] + 0) - (a[k] + 0)
      if (d != 0) printf "    %-24s %6d -> %-6d (%+d)%s\n", k, a[k] + 0, b[k] + 0, d, (nm[k] != "" ? "  " nm[k] : "") }
    for (c in ca) if (!(c in cb)) { sub("^#crash\t", "", c) ; print "    crash gone   " c }
    for (c in cb) if (!(c in ca)) { sub("^#crash\t", "", c) ; print "    crash new    " c }
  }' "$OLD" "$NEW"
exit 0

content.content:
## 1. What changed

The branch was new; nothing was inherited. Four commits: the tests alone (`62a62f94c`, `8166315d4`), the edit (`91ed5d776`), and a follow-up the first distance run asked for (`e995c31c0`). Under Q1 = (a) the rung repaired the Meet Rule pairs one type provides, String's own juxtaposition pair and the declared-type slips, and left every top-level pair of two functional methods to rung O.

**Meet Rule pairs, declarations on the meet (P2's devices M and C, and three more):**
- `Maybe` declares `map[\G\](f: T->G): Maybe[\G\]` and `ivmap[\G\](f: (ZZ32,T)->G): Maybe[\G\]` (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:920-921; the component's bodies at Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1441-1444, `cond` over `Just` and `Nothing` as `Condition`'s bodies do). In the api `Maybe` is the first type below both `Condition` and `ZeroIndexed` (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:917).
- `StandardMutableArrayType` declares `copy():T` (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1466, Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2134), abstract, where `fill` and `tabulate` already meet.
- `SimpleMappedSeqGenerator` declares `map`, answering a `SimpleMappedSeqGenerator` over the composed function (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3554-3555); `SimpleNestedSeqGenerator` declares `map`, answering a `SimpleNestedSeqGenerator` that maps each inner sequential generator, and `nest`, `NestedGenerator`'s body restated (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3635-3638). The precedent is `SimpleSeqFilterGenerator`'s own `seq` (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3584).
- `String`'s juxtaposition: the three functional methods of `String` (`(a:Any, self)`, `(self, b:String)`, `(self, b:Any)`) become three top-level operators with the same bodies (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2440-2443, Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4237-4240). Two functional methods with `self` at different positions satisfy neither the Subtype nor the Incompatibility Rule, and the text admits no meet for them (Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:517-523); as top-level functions the Meet Rule for functions is met by `(String, String)` (:411-415 contrasts the two rules).

**Slips, each declared type set to what its body answers (P2's S and the rest):**
- the api's `AssociativeReduction.lift(r:R)` against `ActualReduction.lift(r:R)` (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1860); the component's `lift(r:Any)` throughout is unchanged.
- the api's `LessThan` and `GreaterThan` `CMP(self, other: LessThan|GreaterThan): TotalComparison`, as the component already declares (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:139, :150).
- `LeftScalarRange.every: BoundedScalarRange`, `LeftScalarRange.atMost` and `RightScalarRange.atMost: FullScalarRange` (Library/RangeInternals.fsi:240, :242, :298; Library/RangeInternals.fss:563, :571, :683), and `RightScalarRange.every: BoundedScalarRange` (Library/RangeInternals.fsi:296, Library/RangeInternals.fss:675), whose body answers a `LeftScalarRange` for a negative stride.
- `FilterGenerator.filter: FilterGenerator[\E\]`, the api's own type (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3568 against Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2101); `MappedGenerator.map: MappedGenerator[\E,G\]` (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3517). Each had declared an object type that the override in `FilterGenerator2` and `SimpleMappedIndexed` could not answer.
- `ConcreteRelationalPredicateCondition[\E\]` extends `RelationalPredicateCondition[\E\]`, not `[\()\]` (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4598); its `relation` and `target` then answer its parent's.
- `SimpleNestedGenerator.seq: SequentialGenerator[\F\]` and `SimplePairGenerator.seq: SequentialGenerator[\(E,F)\]` (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3617, :3659).
- `Array3.shift: Array[\T,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\]` (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1777, Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2881); `Col` and `Row`'s `subarray: Array1[\T,b,s\]` (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2626, :2637). No code constructs a `Col` or a `Row`, so no walk program reaches the last two.
- `EmptyString` and `FlatString`'s `split(): Generator[\String\] = Nothing[\String\]` and `splitWithOffsets(): Generator[\(ZZ32,String)\] = Nothing[\(ZZ32,String)\]` (Library/String.fss:317-318, Library/FlatString.fss:146-147), the empty generator the api's comment asks for (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2382-2390). This is row 356.
- the unary `BIG MAX` returns `T` (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3247; row 472), and the nullary `BIG MINMAX` is a `Comprehension[\T,(T,T),(T,T),AnyMaybe\]`, as `BIG MIN_MIN`'s siblings are (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1951, Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3259-3260; row 473).
- row 483: `UniformDistribution[\T\](range: FullRange[\T\])` (Library/Random.fsi:258, Library/Random.fss:370), so `T` is the range's element type and a `ZZ64` distribution over a `ZZ32` range is refused at construction.
- row 531: `getter avFlat(): RR32 = narrow(asFloat(ssize) / asFloat(numFlat))` (Library/String.fss:508).

**Tests.** New in `ProjectFortress/tests/`: `LibraryMeetDeclarations.fss` (every repaired declaration a program can reach, called with the value it answers, passing before and after, and two values pinned as today's), `BigMinMax.fss`, `SequentialGeneratorMap.fss`, `XXXUniformDistributionRangeType.fss`. Promoted by `git mv`, component renamed, no assertion changed: `XXXStringAvFlatRungV.fss` to `StringAvFlat.fss` (row 531), `XXXFlatStringSplitRungL.fss` to `FlatStringSplit.fss` (row 356, which the split repair turns green). Review-routed.2: `XXXComprisesMeetUncovered.fss` to `XXXComprisesMeetUncoveredWalk.fss` with its component. Review-routed.1: the messages of `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/ComprisesMeetCompiled.fss:18` and `ProjectFortress/tests/ComprisesMeetWalk.fss:18` now say that by the comprises clauses of S and T and U's excludes clause every value of both S and T is a value of V, so V covers their intersection (Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:367-372); the ledger row number left the message, as the register asks; the assertions are unchanged.
## 4. Each device, with the ways not taken

- **`Maybe`'s `map` and `ivmap`, P2's M.** Not taken: making the api's `Condition` extend `ZeroIndexed` as its component does (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1330 against Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:854), with the api's `ivmap` answering a `Condition` as the component's does, which would make `Condition` the meet in the api too. It is batch 7b's precedent of an api matching its component, but it changes the api parents of every `Condition`, `Boolean` among them, and needs more api declarations retyped; the meet declaration is the smaller device and the one P2 measured.
- **`copy` on `StandardMutableArrayType`, P2's C.** Not taken: redeclaring `copy` in each array leaf, the library's way for `copy` until now, which FACTS ("fill takes a value and tabulate a function, both defined where the array diamond meets") records leaves the meet refused.

P2's repair, the parameter declared `TotalComparison`, makes it reached and changes the answer to `true`; deleting the unreachable overload keeps every answer and drops the team's declaration. The section leaves a slip whose repair changes a value walk prints with a row, so neither is built; nothing in the library or the corpora calls `isLeftZero`. Pinned by `LibraryMeetDeclarations.fss` ("today's value"); new row, provisionally 582.
- **The full sequential ranges' `map`, 2.** `CompactFullSeqScalarRange` and `StridedFullSeqScalarRange` inherit `SequentialGenerator`'s and `Indexed`'s `map` (Library/RangeInternals.fsi:418, :491); a declaration on the meet must answer a type below both, and no library type is both an `Indexed` and a `SequentialGenerator` but `Condition`. The library's precedent would be a new object at that meet, as `SimpleMappedIndexed` and `SimpleMappedSeqGenerator` are for theirs, exported from the api for `RangeInternals` to name. Walk answers `SequentialGenerator`'s, sequential and not indexed (`B1 compactseq.map mapped(seq(10,11,12)) seq notindexed`). Pinned in `LibraryMeetDeclarations.fss`; new row, provisionally 583.
- **`SumReduction`'s two `distribute`, 2 R3.** Each declares `PossibleReductionPair[\AnyMaybe\]` against `ActualReduction`'s `PossibleReductionPair[\R\]`, and its body is a `PossibleReductionPair[\AnyMaybe\]` because the component's `ReductionPair[\R,L\]` extends `SomeReductionPair[\L\]` (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3041) where the api's extends `SomeReductionPair[\R\]` (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1850). opr[r:Range[\I\]] : Indexed[\F,I\] = SimpleMappedIndexed[\E,F,I\](g0[r], f0)
    generate[\R\](r: Reduction[\R\], m: F->R): R = g0.generate[\R\](r, m COMPOSE f0)
    seq(self): SimpleMappedSeqIndexed[\E,F,I\] = self
    ivmap[\R\](ff:(I,F)->R): Indexed[\R,I\] = g0.ivmap[\R\](fn (i:I, e:E):R => ff(i, f0(e)))
    map[\G\](f': F->G): SimpleMappedSeqIndexed[\E,G,I\] =
        SimpleMappedSeqIndexed[\E,G,I\](g0, f' COMPOSE f0)
end

(************************************************************
* STRINGS
************************************************************)

trait String extends { StandardTotalOrder[\String\], ZeroIndexed[\Char\], DelegatedIndexed[\Char,ZZ32\] }
             excludes {Number, Char, AnyMultiplicativeRing, AnyList}
    getter size() : ZZ32
    getter asString() : String = self
    getter indices() : CompactFullRange[\ZZ32\] = self.bounds

    getter left(): Maybe[\Char\] = if |self| = 0 then Nothing[\Char\] else Just[\Char\](self.get(0)) end
    getter right(): Maybe[\Char\] = if |self| = 0 then Nothing[\Char\] else Just[\Char\](self.get(self.size-1)) end

    (* This is the "dumb" generator.  It always works, but can be "Big O" inefficient, e.g., for
       CatString trees.  Sub-traits should override it with equivalent but more efficient code. *)
    getter generator() : Generator[\Char\] =
        self.indices.map[\Char\](fn (i:ZZ32):Char => self[i])
    getter asFlatString(): String

    opr |self| : ZZ32 = self.size

    abstract get(i:ZZ32): Char
    abstract asDebugStringIndented(indent: ZZ32): String

    opr CASE_INSENSITIVE_CMP(self, other:String): TotalComparison =
      self.asFlatString CASE_INSENSITIVE_CMP other.asFlatString

    opr CMP(self, other:String): TotalComparison =
      ((BIG LEXICO[i <- 0#(|self| MIN |other|) ] self.get(i) CMP other.get(i)) LEXICO (|self| CMP |other|))

    opr [i:ZZ32]: Char =
        (** As a convenience, we permit LeftRange indexing to go 1 past the bounds
        of the String, returning the empty String, in order to permit some convenient
        String-trimming idioms. **)
        if 0 <= i < |self|
        then self.get(i)
        else
            (* errorPrintln "Index " i " not in bounds " self.bounds *)
            throw IndexOutOfBounds[\ZZ32\](self.bounds,i)
        end

    opr[r0:Range[\ZZ32\]] : String =  do
        r1 = self.bounds.narrowToRange(r0)     (* This will complete r0 if it is incomplete, and throw a bounds exception when necessary *)
        if r1.stride = 1 then
            self.uncheckedSubstring(r1)
        else
            BIG || [i <- r1] self.get(i)
        end
    end

    uncheckedSubstring(r0: Range[\ZZ32\]) : String
    allButLast(): String = self[0#(|self| - 1)]
    allButFirst(): String = self[1:]

    opr ^(self, n: ZZ32): String =
      if n <= 1 then
        if n=1 then self elif n=0 then "" else throw NegativeLength end
      else
        x = (self || self)^(n DIV 2)
        if odd n then x || self else x end
      end

    upto(c: Char): String =
      if c IN self then
        n = BIG MIN[i <- self.indices, self[i]=c] i
        self[ 0#n ]
      else self end

    beyond(c: Char): String =
      if c IN self then
        n = BIG MIN[i <- self.indices, self[i]=c] i
        self[ (n+1): ]
      else "" end

    (** The operator %||% with at least one String argument converts
        to String and concatenates **)
    opr ||(self, b:String):String
    opr ||(self, b:Number):String = self || b.asString
    opr ||(self, c:Char):String
    opr ||(self, b:()):String = self || "()"
    opr ||(self, b:(Any,Any)):String = do (i,j) = b; self || "(" || i || "," j || ")" end
    opr ||(self, b:(Any,Any,Any)):String =
        do (i,j,k) = b; self || "(" || i || "," j || "," k || ")" end
    opr ||(self, b:(Any,Any,Any,Any)):String =
        do (i,j,k,l) = b; self || "(" || i || "," j || "," k || "," l || ")" end
    opr ||(self, b:(Any,Any,Any,Any,Any)):String =
        do (i,j,k,l,m) = b; self || "(" || i || "," j || "," k || "," l || "," m || ")" end
    opr ||(self, b:(Any,Any,Any,Any,Any,Any)):String =
        do (i,j,k,l,m,n) = b; self || "(" || i || "," j || "," k || "," l || "," m || "," n || ")" end
    opr ||(a:Any, self):String = a.asString || self
    opr ||(self, b:Any):String = self || b.asString

    (** The operator %|||% with at least one String argument converts to string,
        then appends with a whitespace separator unless one of the two arguments is
        empty.  If there is an empty argument, the other argument is returned. **)
    opr |||(self, b:String): String =
        if |self| = 0 then b
        elif |b| = 0 then self
        else self || " " || b
        end
    opr |||(self, b:Any): String = self ||| (""||b)
    opr |||(a:Any, self): String = (""||a) ||| self

    (** opr %//% appends a single line separator.  Note that as
        with %||% and %|||% at least one argument must be a String.
        There is a postfix version defined as a top-level operator in
        FortressLibrary that performs string conversion, but the prefix
         version must occur before a String. **)
    opr //(self) : String = newline || self
    opr //(self, a:String): String = self || newline || a
    opr //(self, a:Any): String    = self || newline || a
    opr //(a:Any, self): String    = a || newline || self

    (** opr %///% appends a double line separator.  Note that, as
        with %||% and %|||%, at least one argument must be a String.
        There is a postfix version defined as a top-level operator in
        FortressLibrary that performs string conversion, but the prefix
         version must occur before a String. **)
    opr ///(self) : String = doubleNewline || self
    opr ///(self, a:String): String = self || doubleNewline || a
    opr ///(self, a:Any): String    = self || doubleNewline || a
    opr ///(a:Any, self): String    = a || doubleNewline || self

    abstract writeOn(s: WriteStream): ()

    stats(): StringStats = do
        ss = StringStats()
        ss.collectStatsFor(self)
        ss
    end

    (* Python-style join operator *)
    join[\E\](g:Generator[\E\]):String = g.generate[\Maybe[\String\]\](StringJoinReduction(self), fn(x:E):Maybe[\String\] => Just[\String\]("" x)).getDefault("")

  end String

(* Concatenates arguments with the given separator *)
object StringJoinReduction(s:String) extends Reduction[\Maybe[\String\]\]
    getter asString():String = "StringJoinReduction(" s ")"
    empty():Maybe[\String\] = Nothing[\String\]
    join(a:Maybe[\String\], b:Maybe[\String\]):Maybe[\String\] = do
        if x <- a then
            if y <- b then
                Just[\String\](x || s || y)
            else
                a
            end
        else
            b
        end
    end
end

(** Right now for backward compatibility juxtaposition works like %||% **)
opr juxtaposition(a:Any, b:String):String = (""||a) || b
opr juxtaposition(a:String, b:String):String = a || b
opr juxtaposition(a:String, b:Any):String = a || b

reverse(sequence:String):String = BIG || [c<-sequence.reverse] c

(***********************************************************
* Numeric primitives
************************************************************)

\Trait{Fortress.Core.Any}

\tracingcommands=1\tracingmacros=1

The trait \TYP{Any} is the single root of the type hierarchy; every
object in Fortress has trait \TYP{Any} and therefore every object
implements the methods of this trait.  The immediate subtypes of the trait
\TYP{Any} are \TYP{Object}, \TYP{Tuple}, and \TYP{()}.

\Trait{Fortress.Core.Tuple}
\seclabel{core-tuple}

The trait \TYP{Tuple} is the root of the type hierarchy for all tuple types (see \secref{tuple-types}).  No user-defined object can be a subtype of \TYP{Tuple}.  As with the type \TYP{Object}, the properties of its existing operators are those stated in trait \TYP{Any}.

%trait Tuple extends Any
%    excludes { Object }
%  toString(): String
%end
\begin{Fortress}
\(\KWD{trait}\:\TYP{Tuple} \KWD{extends}\:\TYP{Any}\)\\
{\tt~~~~}\pushtabs\=\+\(    \KWD{excludes} \{\,\TYP{Object}\,\}\)\-\\\poptabs
{\tt~~}\pushtabs\=\+\(  \VAR{toString}()\COLON \TYP{String}\)\-\\\poptabs
\(\KWD{end}\)
\end{Fortress}
\revision{revival-object}{The Working Draft of February 2011 gave
\TYP{Tuple} the same algebraic supertraits as \TYP{Object}, at
\TYP{Tuple}, and said that it uses algebraic constraints to describe its
existing methods. No tuple type extends a trait, so the rule does not
refuse that declaration; it follows \TYP{Object}'s.}


\Method{\EXP{\VAR{toString}()\COLON \TYP{String}}}

The \VAR{toString} method returns a string \EXP{\hbox{\rm``\STR{}''}}
concatenated as follows:
\begin{itemize}
\item If the tuple has just one element, concatenate
\EXP{\hbox{\rm``\STR{tuple}''}}.
\item Concatenate \EXP{\hbox{\rm``\STR{(}''}}.
\item For each element of the tuple, in left-to-right order,
     taking all plain elements before any varargs or keyword
     element, taking any varargs element before any keyword
     element, and taking keyword elements in the order defined
     by the type of the tuple (which may not be the sorted order):
     \begin{itemize}
     \item If this is a plain element,
 concatenate the \VAR{toString} of the element.
     \item If this is a varargs element ``\EXP{e\ldots}'',
 concatenate the \VAR{toString} of \VAR{e} and
 concatenate \EXP{\hbox{\rm``\STR{...}''}}.
     \item If this is a keyword element ``\EXP{\VAR{id} = e}'',
 concatenate the \VAR{toString} of \VAR{id},
 concatenate \EXP{\hbox{\rm``\STR{~=~}''}}, and
 concatenate the \VAR{toString} of \VAR{e}.
     \item If this is the last element of the tuple,
 concatenate \EXP{\hbox{\rm``\STR{)}''}};
          otherwise concatenate ", ".
     \end{itemize}
\end{itemize}

(** Assertion *)
assert(flag:Boolean): () =
    if NOT flag then
        fail("Assertion failed!")
    end

assert(flag: Boolean, failMsg: String): () =
    if NOT flag then
        fail(failMsg)
    end

assert(x:Any, y:Any, failMsg: Any...): () =
    if x =/= y then
        xs = typecase x of
                 x':Object => x'.asDebugString
                 else => "" x
             end
        ys = typecase y of
                 y':Object => y'.asDebugString
                 else => "" y
             end
        msg = xs " =/= " ys "; " (BIG || failMsg)  (* use || here instead of loose juxt *)
        fail(msg)
    end

deny(flag:Boolean): () = assert(NOT flag)

deny(flag: Boolean, failMsg: String): () = assert(NOT flag, failMsg)

deny(x:Any, y:Any, failMsg: Any...): () =
    if x = y then
        xs = typecase x of
                 x':Object => x'.asDebugString
                 else => "" x
             end
        ys = typecase y of
                 y':Object => y'.asDebugString
                 else => "" y
             end
        msg = xs " = " ys "; " (BIG || failMsg)
        fail(msg)
    end

shouldRaise⟦Ex extends Exception⟧ (expr: ()→()): () = do
    raised = try
        expr()
        false
      catch x
        Ex => true (* This is what we hope for *)
      forbid Exception

native component Reflect

export Reflect

import List.{...}
import Set.{...}
import Tuple.{...}

private language = "java"
private package = "com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim"

(******************************************************************************)
(* External interfaces *)

(** A reflected type object. **)
trait Type extends StandardTotalOrder[\Type\]
           comprises {GenericType, ObjectOrTraitType, ArrowType, TupleType,
                      RestType, BottomType}
    getter asString(): String =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.Reflect$ToString")

    (** Two type objects are same if types represented by them are same;
        the comparison is nominal and correctly distinguishes different
        types with a same name but in the different APIs. **)
    opr =(self, other:Type): Boolean =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.Reflect$Eq")

    (** An arbitrary comparison operator to allow the construction of a set of
        types. **)
    opr <(self, other:Type): Boolean =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.Reflect$Less")

    (** Returns true if it is a subtype of given type. **)
    opr SUBTYPEOF(self, other:Type): Boolean =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.Reflect$SubtypeOf")

    (** Returns true if it is a supertype of given type. **)
    opr SUPERTYPEOF(self, other:Type): Boolean =
        other SUBTYPEOF self

    (** Calculates a join of two types, that is, a minimal set of common
        supertypes. It is "minimal" in the sense that it will transitively
        generate all other supertypes, including %Any%. **)
    join0(self, other:Type): ReflectCollection =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.Reflect$Join")
    join(self, other:Type): Generator[\Type\] = join0(self, other).specific[\Type\]()

    (** Calculates a meet of two types, that is, a minimal set of common
        subtypes. It is "minimal" in the sense that it will transitively
        generate all other subtypes, including %BOTTOM%. **)
    meet0(self, other:Type): ReflectCollection =
        builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim.Reflect$Meet")
    meet(self, other:Type): Generator[\Type\] = meet0(self, other).specific[\Type\]()
end

content.content:
\paragraph{The Meet Rule for Functions:}
Suppose that $\f(\Ps)$ and $\f(\Qs)$ are two function
declarations in a single scope
such that neither $\Ps$ nor $\Qs$ is a subtype of the other and $\Ps$ and
$\Qs$ are not incompatible with one another.
Let $\mathpzc{S}$ be the set of types that $\Ps$ defines coercions from
and $\mathpzc{T}$ be the set of types that $\Qs$ defines coercions from.
$\f(\Ps)$ and $\f(\Qs)$ are a valid overloading if
there is a declaration $\f(\Ps \inter \Qs)$ in the scope.

all of the following hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item
either $\Ps \excludes \Qs$ or there is a declaration $\f(\Ps \inter
\Qs)$ in the scope,
and
\item
either $\Ps \morespecific \Qs$ or $\Qs \morespecific \Ps$ or for all
$\Ps' \in \mathpzc{S}$ and $\Qs' \in \mathpzc{T}$ one of the two
conditions holds:
\begin{itemize}
\item
$\Ps' \excludes \Qs'$, or
\item
there is a declaration $\f(\Ps' \inter \Qs')$ in the scope.
\end{itemize}
\end{itemize}

Where the Meet Rule for functions asks for a declaration $\f(\Ps \inter \Qs)$ in
the scope, it is also satisfied by declarations in the scope whose parameter
types are each a subtype of both $\Ps$ and $\Qs$ and together cover
\paragraph{The Meet Rule for Functional Methods:}
Suppose that $\f(\Ps)$ and $\f(\Qs)$ are two functional method
declarations occurring in trait or object declarations or object expressions
such that neither $\Ps$ nor $\Qs$ is a subtype of the other and $\Ps$ and $\Qs$
are not incompatible with one another.  Let $\f(\Ps)$ and $\f(\Qs)$
have self parameters at $i$ and $j$ respectively.
$\f(\Ps)$ and $\f(\Qs)$ are a valid
overloading if all of the following hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item
$i = j$
\item if there exists a trait or object $C$
that provides both $\f(\Ps)$ and $\f(\Qs)$ then $\Ps \neq \Qs$ and
there is a declaration $\f(\Ps \inter \Qs)$ provide by $C$
having self parameter at $i$.
\end{itemize}

Also, let $\mathpzc{S}$ be the set of types that $\Ps$
defines coercions from and $\mathpzc{T}$ be the set of types that
$\Qs$ defines coercions from.  $\f(\Ps)$ and $\f(\Qs)$ are a valid
overloading if all of the following hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item
$i = j$
\item
either $\Ps \excludes \Qs$ or if there exists a trait or object $C$
that provides both $\f(\Ps)$ and $\f(\Qs)$ then $\Ps \neq \Qs$ and
there is a declaration $\f(\Ps \inter \Qs)$ provide by $C$, and
\item
either $\Ps \morespecific \Qs$ or $\Qs \morespecific \Ps$ or
for all $\Ps' \in \mathpzc{S}$ and
$\Qs' \in \mathpzc{T}$ one of the two conditions holds:
\begin{itemize}
\item
$\Ps' \excludes \Qs'$, or
\item
there is a declaration $\f(\Ps' \inter \Qs')$ provided by $C$.
\end{itemize}
\end{itemize}

As for functions, where this rule asks for a declaration
$\f(\Ps \inter \Qs)$ provided by $C$, it is also satisfied by declarations
provided by $C$, having self parameter at $i$, whose parameter types are each a
subtype of both $\Ps$ and $\Qs$ and together cover $\Ps \inter \Qs$; the case
does not apply to the condition on the types from which $\Ps$ and $\Qs$ define
coercions.
\revision{revival-meet}{The Working Draft of February 2011 asked here, as for
functions, for a declaration on the intersection itself.}

Notice that the Meet Rule for functional methods requires the self
parameters of two overloaded declarations to be in the same position.
This requirement guarantees that no ambiguity is caused by the
position of the self parameter.  Two declarations which differ in the
position of the self parameter must satisfy either the Subtype Rule or
the Incompatibility Rule to be a valid overloading.

Functional method declarations can overload with function declaraions.
A valid overloading between a functional method declaration and
a function declaration is
determined by applying the (more restrictive) Meet Rule for functions
to both declarations.
